summary.summary: South Ribble is effectively debt-free: gross debt at 31 March 2026 was just £42k of finance leases, with the £25.1m capital financing requirement met entirely from the council's own cash and no external borrowing taken in the year. Investments stood at £22.3m at year end (average daily balance £37.1m, earning £1,503k at 3.63%), including £11m of term deposits with Blackpool and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole councils, and financing costs are a modest 3.28% of the net revenue stream. The trend to watch is slow cash erosion: average balances fell 16.6% year-on-year and interest earned dropped 33% as capital spending is funded internally, while the CFR rose from £19.7m to £25.1m. All prudential indicators and counterparty limits were complied with.

news_drafts.headline: South Ribble revises 2026/27 unsupported borrowing to £7.5m from £11.6m, with later years rising to £12m
news_drafts.lead:
South Ribble Council's capital programme now shows £7.517m of unsupported borrowing for 2026/27, against £11.639m when the programme was approved in March 2026. The Quarter 2 update goes to Cabinet on 18 November. Unsupported borrowing is borrowing taken on without government support behind it.

The 2026/27 figure is reduced by £1.19m of slippage, meaning spending moved to later years, and by £6.918m of Quarter 2 variations. The same £1.19m of slippage appears in the later years. The borrowing figure for 2027/28 and future years rises from £6.521m, the position at four months to July 2026, to £12.039m. The Quarter 2 variations add £4.328m to that figure, and slippage adds the £1.19m.

The papers are Appendix A to the report, the capital programme. The table sets out the March approval, the changes made during the year and the revised totals for each period.

news_drafts.headline: South Ribble's 2026/27 unsupported borrowing falls to £7.5m from £11.6m approved in March
news_drafts.lead:
South Ribble Council's capital programme now includes £7.517m of unsupported borrowing for 2026/27, against £11.639m approved at the March 2026 council meeting. Unsupported borrowing is borrowing for capital schemes that has no government support behind it. The revised figure is the council's position at 30 September 2026, set out in the capital programme appendix to the quarter 2 report for the Corporate, Performance and Budget Scrutiny Committee meeting on 16 November.

The appendix shows slippage of £1.19m and a quarter 2 variation of £6.918m against the 2026/27 line. For 2027/28 and future years the figure moves the other way. It rises from £6.521m to £12.039m, after the same £1.19m of slippage and a quarter 2 increase of £4.328m.

The paper does not give reasons for the variations or name the schemes affected.

news_drafts.headline: South Ribble commits £20,000 borrowing for affordable housing acquisition
news_drafts.lead: South Ribble Council has approved a capital budget to acquire a three or four-bedroom family home using Section 106 contributions — money from developers building new homes locally. The council will use £250,000 from the Section 106 agreement and borrow £20,000 to meet the £270,000 purchase price, creating an annual debt service cost of roughly £2,000. The property will generate £10,200 per year in rental income, which the council's chief finance officer confirms should cover both the borrowing costs and day-to-day running expenses such as repairs and maintenance, making the investment self-financing. Officers have flagged that the Section 106 agreement includes time limits for spending the contributions and circumstances where unspent money becomes repayable, creating a compliance risk the council has decided to accept.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation Reserves are forecast to fall from £360k to nil, with the full £360k moved in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The line shows an opening balance of £360k and a movement of £360k. The closing balance and committed and uncommitted columns are all shown as nil.
findings.matters: A council closing out a reorganisation reserve is showing how one-off transition funding has been fully applied, which other councils preparing for similar changes would want to know.
findings.figures: £360k opening; £360k movement; nil forecast at 31 March 2027

findings.headline: Forced Migration reserve is forecast at £941k at 31 March 2027, all of it committed to future years.
findings.detail: The reserve opens at £1,114k, with movements of £178k and £5k. The paper shows the full £941k closing balance committed and no uncommitted balance.
findings.matters: A council holding a reserve for a demand pressure with no uncommitted balance has no spare capacity if the pressure grows, which other councils facing similar pressures would want to compare.
findings.figures: £1,114k opening; £178k movement; £5k movement; £941k forecast at 31 March 2027; £941k committed; nil uncommitted

findings.headline: Short Life Operational Assets reserve falls from £2,214k to £1,764k at 31 March 2027, with the whole closing balance committed to future years.
findings.detail: The reserve shows a £450k movement during 2026/27. The paper shows £1,764k committed to future years and no uncommitted balance.
findings.matters: A reserve with no uncommitted balance is fully allocated to future operational asset costs, which shows how much of a council's capital-related reserve capacity is already spoken for.
findings.figures: £2,214k opening; £450k movement; £1,764k forecast at 31 March 2027; £1,764k committed; nil uncommitted

findings.headline: Budget Equalisation Reserve is forecast at £1,634k at 31 March 2027, with £450k committed to future years.
findings.detail: The reserve opens at £2,016k and shows movements of £447k and £65k. The uncommitted balance on the line is shown as £1,184k.
findings.matters: The budget equalisation reserve is the buffer that smooths funding volatility, so its remaining balance and commitments show how much a council can absorb a shortfall in future years.
findings.figures: £2,016k opening; £447k movement; £65k movement; £1,634k forecast at 31 March 2027; £450k committed; £1,184k uncommitted

findings.headline: General Fund Balance is forecast to rise from £4,333k to £4,595k at 31 March 2027.
findings.detail: The general fund balance line shows a movement of £262k, taking the balance to £4,595k. The paper shows the full balance as uncommitted.
findings.matters: A rising general fund balance is the council's last line of defence against unplanned overspends, so a finance director elsewhere would compare its trajectory with their own.
